title: Phaladeepika
author: Mantreswara
known_defects: Chapter 8, printed p.96: the section heading 'JUPITER' is run onto the end of Mercury's 12th-house paragraph. Corpus preserved as printed; card PD.08.Mercury.12 tightens its span and records why.

Chapter 8, verses 34-35: the Notes worked example and verse 35 appear to disagree about whether proximity to the Bhava-Madhya increases or decreases a placement's effect. Not yet extracted; needs adjudication.

Chapter 8, printed p.99-101: a transcribed horoscope chart and an editorial aside about Swami Ramakrishna Paramahamsa sit inside the Saturn section. Both are tier-3 apparatus and are excluded from rule extraction.
Chapter 9, printed p.108-109: two transcribed horoscope charts and a worked example ending in an aside about Abraham Lincoln. Tier-3 apparatus, excluded from rule extraction.

Chapter 9, verse 14 vs its Notes: Mantreswara says an exalted planet makes the native a ruler of the Earth; the translator's Notes say plainly that it does not. Both are encoded, as PD.09.Dignity.Exalted (tier 1) and PD.09.Dignity.Exalted.Notes (tier 2), and the disagreement is preserved rather than resolved.

Chapter 10, verses 3(a)-(e): the effect ('The native loses his wife') is printed once, in a governing sentence, and the five dispositions follow as separate paragraphs. A card can quote only one contiguous span, so the five are recorded inert and linked to PD.10.WifeLoss.List by 'extends'. Their conditions are exact and would fire correctly; what is missing is the ability to quote two spans.

Chapter 10, verse 5: 'Mars and Saturn in the 7th from the Venus and Moon' counts houses from a graha, not from the lagna. The engine has one reference frame, so PD.10.MarsSaturn.SeventhFromVenusMoon is recorded inert with a condition that is deliberately not the verse's.

Chapter 10, verse 8: two rules distinguished only by the sex of the native, which the birth record does not carry. Both conditions are exactly expressible; both cards are inert so the engine cannot assert a sex-specific rule for every chart.
Chapter 10, verses 4 and 15: the same rule stated twice, the second attributed ('So say the men well versed in the science of Astrology') and carrying an extra condition. Both encoded; not merged.

Chapter 9, verses 13-20: universally quantified over the grahas ('a planet', not a named one) or over other rules. The condition language has no variables, so these eleven cards are recorded and marked inert. The knowledge is encoded and verified; it does not yet fire.

Chapter 1, verse 8: the verse names four Prishtodaya signs (Taurus, Cancer, Aries, Capricorn) and two Ubhayodaya signs (Gemini, Pisces); the very next sentence names five Prishtodaya signs, adding Sagittarius, and one Ubhayodaya sign, dropping Pisces. The two disagree as printed. Both are encoded, as PD.01.Rising.Verse8 and PD.01.Rising.DayNight, linked by contradicts. Neither is corrected.

Chapter 1, verse 7 trailer: the biped/quadruped/centiped/watery classification is a four-column table whose columns the scan interleaved into uneven rows. PD.01.SignBodyForm.Table encodes the quote but not the assignment, and is inert pending human verification against the printed page.

Chapter 1, verse 6 Notes: three positions on the exaltation of Rahu and Ketu -- Mantreswara silent, Sarvarth Chintamani (Gemini/Sagittarius), Brihat Parasara Hora Sastra (Taurus/Scorpio). All three encoded and linked by contradicts. The engine currently assumes no nodal exaltation, which this records as unsourced rather than wrong.

Chapter 1, verse 4 trailer: two definitions of Rasi-Sandhi, Mantreswara’s (the end portions of Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces) and an unnamed dissenting view (the end portions of all signs). Both encoded.

Chapter 1, verse 14: the ninth-house significations carry a parenthetical dispute about whether the father is read from the 9th or the 10th house. Preserved inside the quote of PD.01.HouseSignifications.H09.

Chapter 2, verses 21-22: the seven-graha natural friendship table is four columns the scan interleaved past reconstruction -- the Sun's row reads 'Sun Moon, Mercury Venus Mars Saturn Jupiter', with all six other grahas present but no column boundaries, and one row carries a literal '-----'. PD.02.Friendship.NaturalTable encodes the quote and is inert pending human verification. Reconstructing it would mean importing the classical table from outside the quote.

Chapter 2, verse 25 vs verse 1: verse 1 makes the Sun the significator of the father without qualification; verse 25 makes it so only for a day birth and gives the father to Saturn for a night birth. Both encoded, linked by contradicts, neither corrected.
Chapter 2, verses 30-32: the substances table prints 'Cold' for Jupiter where 'Gold' is expected. Transcribed as printed.

Chapter 2, verse 27: the list of ruling deities is printed with a full stop after 'Yama' and continues 'Serpent Adhishesha and Braham respectively', so the seven names straddle an apparent sentence boundary. Transcribed as printed; the graha-to-deity mapping is left to the quote rather than parsed.

Chapter 2, verse 36 Notes: the combustion orbs are stated here (Moon 12 degrees, Mars 17, Mercury 14 direct and 12 retrograde, Jupiter 11, Venus 10 and 8 retrograde, Saturn 15). The registry had recorded these as doctrine whose source was not yet located.

Chapter 2, verse 36: a horary rule about the water level in a reservoir sits among the natal material. Its condition is an ordinary Moon placement and would fire on a birth chart, so PD.02.Prashna.ReservoirWater is inert pending a branch distinction.

Chapter 2, verses 21-22 (printed p.22): the natural-friendship table prints Mercury under both the Friend and the Neutral column for the Moon row, and prints '-----' (no enemy) in the Moon's Enemy column. Confirmed by direct visual inspection of a high-zoom render of the source PDF page (not the OCR/pdf_text line dump, which had merely flattened the four columns into extraction order and made the table look damaged when it is not). Encoded as printed in PD.02.Friendship.NaturalTable, including the duplication; neither corrected nor resolved.

Chapter 6 (YOGAS), slice 1 only (2026-08-19): the five Pancha Mahapurusha Yogas (verses 1-4, printed p.55-57) are encoded as PD.06.Ruchaka/.Bhadra/.Hamsa/.Malavya/.Sasa, each a two-span card quoting its own naming clause and effect verse. Chapter 6 is deliberately NOT added to chapters_extracted yet -- most of the chapter (verses 5 onward) remains unencoded and is still covered by the whole-chapter chapter:phaladeepika.06 backlog entry. Verse 9's blanket strength caveat is recorded once (passage:phaladeepika.06.p009) rather than duplicated across the five cards. The closing sentence at p.56-57 (also true from the Moon; compounds with two-to-five such yogas at once) is deferred (passage:phaladeepika.06.p022) rather than widened or invented. Four illustrative horoscope clusters in this range (Stalin; Dr. Radhakrishnan; Moti Lal Nehru) are tier-3 apparatus, excluded exactly as chapters 8-9 excluded theirs.

Chapter 6, slice 2 (2026-08-19): the twelve house-wise yogas of vv. 44-56 (Chamara, Dhenu, Shaurya, Jaladhi, Chhattra, Astra [6th], Kama, Astra [8th], Bhagya, Khyati, Parijata, Musala) are encoded as PD.06.<Name> / PD.06.Astra.H06 / PD.06.Astra.H08, one repeating template (a benefic occupying or aspecting the house; its own lord, not combust, in an auspicious house in exaltation or own sign) carried forward from item 1's full statement into items 2-12's 'similarly disposed' shorthand exactly as the text instructs. Astra Yoga is printed twice, for the 6th and 8th houses, and stays distinguished by house. The Notes defending the 6th-house member (a dusthana lord can still be auspicious) is reference doctrine, PD.06.Astra.H06.Notes, discursive rather than a further testable condition. The Sunapha/Anapha/Durudhara cluster (vv. 5-7) was investigated for slice 2 and set aside: the printed text states only that the three yogas collectively arise from planets in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon (confirmed against a direct render of PDF page 58, not just the extraction) without ever stating which sub-condition names which yoga, so the three cannot be individually conditioned without importing the convention from outside this passage. Left for a later slice as passage:phaladeepika.06.p031.

Chapter 6, slice 3 (2026-08-19), vv. 14-27: Mahabhagya (sex-scoped, day/night birth read as the Sun above/below the horizon -- houses 7-12 vs 1-6 from the lagna, an engine choice no authority disputes, recorded rather than asserted by the verse), Kesari, Sakata (with its cancellation clause), Adhama/Sama/Varishtha (from the Sun; safely split by the verse's own "respectively", unlike the still-deferred Sunapha/Anapha/Durudhara cluster), Amala, Subhamala/Asubhamala ("Subnamala" in the naming clause vs "Sumala" in the effect verse, confirmed against printed page 65 and preserved as two different printed spellings), Lakshmi, Gouri and Saraswati Yogas encoded. Vasumati Yoga (PD.06.Vasumati) is inert: universally quantified over the variable-membership set of benefic grahas, which the condition language cannot express (dep.universal-quantification, newly registered, not implemented -- a new combinator, not an extension of an existing one). Pushkala Yoga (PD.06.Pushkala) is inert on three independent grounds: dep.strength, an unresolved "together in a Kendra" reading (conjoined vs. each independently), and an undefined "Adhimitra" friendship tier beyond dep.dignity-friendship's three; confirmed against printed page 64 before recording. Four illustrative horoscope clusters and the Indira Gandhi Mahabhagya note are tier-3 apparatus, excluded.

Chapter 6, vv. 57-69 (Milestone 25), the twelve dusthana-lord yogas (passage:phaladeepika.06.p202): one governing reference card, PD.06.DusthanaLord.General (v.57), plus twelve firing cards, PD.06.DusthanaLord.<Name>, one per house -- the same one-repeating-template idiom as the vv.44-56 house-wise family (slice 2), a dusthana-lord-or-malefic template instead of a benefic one. The general reading (any of the 6th/8th/12th lords posited in house N, or house N occupied/aspected by a malefic, forms yoga N) is not imported from outside the passage: v.63 and v.65 both restate it in full for N=6 and N=8, and the translator's own note at p.231 independently cross-checks it. The house-10 member is PD.06.DusthanaLord.Duryoga, not PD.06.Duryoga, to stay distinguishable from the unrelated v.70 pair (Milestone 24) -- the exact collision this passage's own deferred.json entry flagged in advance. "Daridra Yoga" (v.57's naming list, para. 203) and "Daridrya Yoga" (v.68's own naming sentence) are two printed spellings of the 11th-house member, preserved as printed (card id and predicts.yoga follow v.68's own spelling, since that is this card's own quote); "VimalaYoga" (no space, para. 204) and "Vlmla Yoga" (v.69) are likewise two printed forms of the 12th-house member's name, the second an evident scan defect, both transcribed as printed. Parashara's own nine-combination breakdown (paras 220-228, quoted by the translator) is encoded as ten further firing cards, PD.06.Parashara.<Lord>In<House>, linked to PD.06.DusthanaLord.Harsha/.Sarala/.Vimala by contradicts (five pairs, two polarity:qualified) or parallel_of (two pairs) per a plain reading of each combination's own stated valence against the Mantreswara card's blanket claim -- not forced uniformly to contradiction. Item (5) (8th lord in 8th) splits into an unconditional base sentence ("will be longlived", parallel with Sarala) and a genuinely conditional "if weak" sentence (PD.06.Parashara.EighthLordInEighth.Weak, qualifying it), since the source states two different things under two different conditions. Item (6)'s trailing "more so, if there be additionally a malefic in the said house" is quoted but not independently conditioned: it needs a distinct-from-the-already-bound-lord quantifier the condition language does not have, and a single clause does not justify inventing one (see PD.06.Parashara.EighthLordInTwelfth's own note). Dr. B.V. Raman's commentary (paras 229-230) and the translator's closing remarks on verse 57's malefic clause and the three yogas' absence from Brihat Jataka/Saravali/Jataka Parijata (paras 231-232) remain tier-3 discursive apparatus, restating Parashara's side without adding independently testable doctrine, and are not quoted by any card. PD.06.Astra.H06.Notes (slice 2), which had already quoted a translator aside forward-referencing "Verse 57 of this very chapter" before this slice existed, is updated to corroborate PD.06.DusthanaLord.General now that the forward reference is resolved. Real charts exercising a genuine chart-dependent contradiction, qualification and parallel-authority relationship (all three, both sides activated, `unresolved`) were found by scanning ~1,700 nativities across four cities, 1950-2010, and are pinned in Engine/tests/test_chapter_six_dusthana_lord.py rather than left to hand-constructed fixtures alone.

Chapter 6, vv. 39-41 (Milestone 27), the seven-planets-in-N-signs family (passage:phaladeepika.06.p168): seven firing cards, PD.06.Vallaki/.Dharma/.Hasha/.Kendra/.Shula/.Yuga/.Gola, one per item -- each item is its own self-contained paragraph (condition, yoga name and effect all stated together), unlike the vv.44-56/vv.57-69 house-wise families' shared-template idiom, so no governing/reference card carries a condition. Confirmed against a direct 300dpi render of printed pp.73-74; no known defect, no Notes, no translator commentary on this passage -- the extraction is exactly what the render shows. Item (1)'s naming clause gives the yoga two names in the same sentence ('known as Vallaki. This is also called Veena Yoga.'); the card id and predicts.yoga use the first-given name, the second recorded in the note, not a printed-spelling defect like Subhamala/Asubhamala's. Needed one new engine fact, seven_graha_sign_count(n) (Engine/facts.py::_seven_graha_sign_count, dep.seven-graha-sign-count), because nothing in the prior vocabulary counted distinct signs occupied by a fixed set of bodies. Which nine grahas count as 'the seven' is read from a new reference card, PD.06.SevenGrahas (predicts.relation='seven_grahas'), quoting the phrase 'the seven planets from Sun to Saturn' as a strict substring of PD.06.Vallaki's own span -- not a Python literal, per Engine/doctrine.py's standing discipline that a fixed member set is doctrine, not an engine choice. The seven cards are linked to each other by parallel_of (mutually exclusive by construction: a chart has exactly one distinct-sign count for these seven bodies), the same relationship PD.06.Varishtha/.Sama/.Adhama and PD.06.Lakshmi/.Gouri already carry for a same-book sibling family. A direct ephemeris sweep (not a birth-record sweep, since sign occupancy depends only on longitude) of 219,132 daily instants across 1800-01-02 to 2399-12-20 -- the full range the vendored Swiss Ephemeris data covers -- found every one of the seven counts occurring naturally, n=5 most common (43.3%) and n=1 rarest (4 days in 600 years, including 1962-02-04/05, the widely reported February 1962 'Great Conjunction'). One real chart per count, from the 1950-2035 window, is pinned in Engine/tests/test_chapter_six_sign_count.py; every one fires exactly the matching card and no other, and no chart -- real or constructed -- was found or can occur where zero or more than one of the seven fires, which is the family's own partition property rather than an engine guarantee.

Chapter 19 (Milestone 30), dep.dasa -- the Vimshottari mahadasa engine: v.2's nine-graha order/period-years table and the Krittika-groups-of-nine nakshatra cycle (PD.19.VimshottariPeriods, relation `vimshottari_periods`, read by a new `Doctrine.vimshottari_periods` accessor); v.4's naming of a dasa-year as a solar year, with no printed day-count, so `Engine/dasa.py::DASA_YEAR_DAYS` (365.25) is engine arithmetic rather than doctrine (PD.19.YearDefinition, not consulted by any accessor); and vv.18-26, the nine per-graha Vimshottari effect verses, as nine firing cards PD.19.Dasa.<Graha>, conditioned on a new literal predicate `mahadasa_lord(graha)`. Verses 5-17 are deliberately NOT encoded as firing cards: v.17's own Notes say outright that vv.5-17's effects 'should not apply to Vimsottari dasa system' (they belong to other dasa systems this project does not build), so encoding them against `mahadasa_lord` would attach the wrong doctrine to a computed window; recorded instead as a deferred passage quoting that disclaimer. Verse 3's balance-at-birth dispute is preserved rather than resolved: the root verse states Mantreswara's own division-by-60 shortcut (PD.19.BalanceMethod.Mantreswara), and the same verse's Notes reject it ('not correct as the total number of ghatikas are not always 60') before giving the degree/longitude proportional method the engine actually computes with (PD.19.BalanceMethod, two-span across the p.175/176 page break) -- verified against the Notes' own worked example (Moon at Cancer 13°12', 9°52' elapsed in Pushyami, Saturn's balance 4y11m8d) in Engine/tests/test_dasa.py, not a synthetic case. The two balance-method cards are linked by `contradicts`, documentary only: neither ever fires as a claim (both justify a computation rather than assert something about a nativity), so the link is on record in the store and in this note but does not surface in a per-chart consultation -- Engine.adjudicate only reports a declared link once at least one side has an activated claim. PD.19.Dasa.Rahu and PD.19.Dasa.Ketu (vv.21, 25) are each two-span quotes, crossing the p.179/180 and p.180/181 page breaks respectively, the same dep.multi-span-quote pattern PD.19.BalanceMethod uses. Mahadasa only: no antardasa sub-division formula is printed anywhere in ch. 19 or ch. 20 (both state antardasa *effects*, never the arithmetic), so none is built -- inventing one would be exactly the speculative vocabulary this store's own discipline forbids. Every one of the nine `mahadasa_lord` facts fires on every chart (the birth moment fixes the whole 120-year sequence, not 'now'), so a chart's dasa timeline needs no query-date input anywhere in the pipeline, the same way its planetary placements are fixed regardless of when the report is read. Chapter 20 (dasa/antardasa effects by house lord) is left deferred and is the natural next milestone: `dep.dasa` and `dep.lord-of-house` are now both implemented.

Chapter 20 (Milestone 31), the Mahadasa-scoped slice of dasa/antardasa effects by house lord: reading the full chapter (63 verses, not just the deferred-summary) found no Antardasa order or duration arithmetic anywhere in it either -- verses invoking antardasa name which related planet's antardasa matters and what effect it carries, never how long one lasts or in what order the nine sub-lords run, so no Antardasa mechanism is built. vv.2-13 (strong house-lord dasa effects, houses 1-12) and vv.15-20 (weak house-lord dasa effects, split at the paragraph boundary into 12 house-specific cards since v.15 through v.20 print two houses per verse, unlike vv.2-13's one-per-verse pattern) are gated by v.14's own local disposition criterion -- own sign/exaltation/retrograde and not in a dusthana = auspicious; inimical sign/debilitation/combust or in a dusthana = adverse -- encoded as a new predicate, `dasa_disposition` (Engine/facts.py::_dasa_disposition, PD.20.Disposition), deliberately NOT reusing chapter 4's `strength` verdict because that verdict (vv.4-5) carries no own-sign, no inimical-sign and no dusthana-placement clause and is verifiably narrower than what v.14 states (see concept:strength-criterion-scope). A graha satisfying both of v.14's clauses at once (e.g. retrograde and combust together) gets no verdict, mirroring `_strength`'s own retrograde+combust collision discipline. v.22's first two sentences (Vargottama favourable/mixed in dasa) reuse the existing `vargottama` predicate (dep.varga, Milestone 29) unconditionally; its third sentence (6th/8th/12th lord's antardasa) is antardasa-scoped and deferred. v.40's first sentence (2nd/7th maraka-house lord or occupant, 'powerful', dies in dasa) is encoded reusing the existing chapter-4 `strength` verdict, since this verse states no local criterion of its own the way v.14 does; its second sentence (8th/12th lord weak, death in antardasa of either) is antardasa-scoped and deferred. v.41 ('Parasara's opinion') is encoded as seven cards: kendra-lord dasa adverse-if-benefic/auspicious-if-malefic (joined via a shared `?h` between `lord_of_house` and `house_class`, the same pattern PD.06.DusthanaLord.* uses), trikona-lord dasa favourable, 3rd/6th/11th-lord dasa evil, 8th-and-lagna-same-lord dasa auspicious, and Sun/Moon-as-8th-lord dasa good (two literal per-graha cards, mirroring PD.19.Dasa.<Graha>'s own style). A genuine intra-book discrepancy was found and preserved rather than resolved: v.41 explicitly parenthesizes 'trikonas (1,5,9)', but the existing PD.01.HouseClass.Trikona reference card (ch.1 v.18) defines Trikona as houses 5,9 only in this same book, classifying the Ascendant as `kendra` instead -- PD.20.Parasara.TrikonaLord's condition uses this verse's own explicit house numbers (1,5,9) directly rather than the `house_class` lookup, the most literal reading of what this specific verse states. Similarly, PD.20.Parasara.UpachayaLordEvil uses the verse's own explicit list (3,6,11), not the broader existing `upachaya` class (3,6,10,11) -- house 10 is deliberately excluded, matching the verse's own wording. v.43-44 ('no effect from house-ownership during his dasa and his OWN antar dasa... it is only in the antar dasas of [related] planets that the original planet will in his main dasa manifest his effect') was investigated directly against the source and read as an antardasa-scoped refinement of WHEN within a mahadasa the vv.2-21 effects manifest, not a denial that they exist -- no `contradicts` link was drawn against vv.2-21/v.41, since the source's own adjacent sentence (v.44) resolves the apparent tension rather than leaving it genuinely unresolved. Everything else in the chapter -- the antardasa-relational cluster (vv.22c,23,28,29,42,43-44,45-54), the transit-during-dasa cluster (vv.31-32,34-39,59-62, needs `dep.transit`, chapter 26 itself still unencoded), the 'weakest of N candidates' death-timing cluster (vv.31,32,55,58, needs a comparator mechanism this store does not have), v.30's percentage-weighted dignity effects (hits the project's standing no-invented-numeric-weighting refusal directly), vv.56-57's degree-position dasa-quality doctrine (Arohini/Avarohini/Madhya/Adhama, real and buildable but needs a new predicate, not built this milestone), vv.25-26/33 (need sign classifications -- Urdhvamukha, Shirshodaya/Ubhayodaya/Prishtodaya -- this store has not encoded), v.21's cross-chapter attribution meta-rule, v.24's ordinal-dasa-position clauses (explicitly excluded from this milestone though buildable later from the already-computed mahadasa sequence with zero antardasa), v.27's non-lord-specific graha dignity/house-placement dasa effects (buildable with existing predicates but outside this milestone's agreed scope), and v.63/the closing translator Notes -- is deferred and tracked in Rules/deferred.json, not silently dropped.
